=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- .claude/commands/audit-plans.md
  Line or code reference: Report format "In-flight /implement-plan-claude work: <implement-plan <slug> (log: <Status:>, stage <Stage:>), PR #M (open, files: ...)>  (or: none / logs only — GitHub UNAVAILABLE)"
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
  PROBLEM: The report format line assumes every in-flight /implement-plan-claude project has a log with Status: and Stage: fields. Step 6(b) says a PR whose slug cannot be resolved counts as its own in-flight project, but such a PR has no log, no slug, and no stage, so the implementer has nothing to fill into the Status: or Stage: slots. The existing "(or: none / logs only — GitHub UNAVAILABLE)" alternative covers GitHub being down altogether but not GitHub being available when the PR has no log.
  WHY: If an implementer encounters a claude/implement-plan-* PR whose slug cannot be resolved from the branch name or changed files, they have no Status/Stage to report in the template. This is a minor gap in the template; the conflict footprint still works, but the human-readable report line would be incomplete.

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- .claude/commands/audit-plans.md,workflow-templates/.claude/commands/audit-plans.md
  Line or code reference: Step 6, "Set aside plans that are already in flight." bullet (new lines ~33-37 in the modified file; same text in the workflow-templates copy)
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
  PROBLEM: The bullet says "an in-flight `/implement-plan-claude` log's `Plan:` line (or an unlogged PR's slug) points at it" — the parenthetical treats a PR's slug as if it points at the source plan, but the slug identifies the project (and the `docs/implement-plan/<slug>.md` log file), not the plan. The `Plan:` line is what names the plan; an unlogged PR has no log, so the slug does not point at any plan. For a candidate plan to be set aside, an implementer needs the plan's path, not the project's slug.
  WHY: For a new project's first phase PR (the case the description explicitly calls out: "A new project's first phase PR has no log on the default branch yet"), the implementer can determine that an `/implement-plan-claude` project exists and is in flight, but cannot determine which plan it is implementing. The set-aside step therefore silently skips such projects (since the rule that "the slug points at it" cannot be satisfied literally), even though they would otherwise satisfy the criterion "already being implemented". The instruction needs an additional rule for the unlogged-PR case (e.g. either set aside no plan — rely on the conflict screen — or accept a `slug → plan` naming convention and document it).

- .claude/commands/audit-plans.md,workflow-templates/.claude/commands/audit-plans.md
  Line or code reference: Step 6, "Enumerate in-flight `/implement-plan-claude` work", bullet (b) Open PRs (new lines ~30-33 in the modified file; same text in the workflow-templates copy)
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
  PROBLEM: The branch examples "(`claude/implement-plan-<slug>-phase-<n>`, `-validation-fix-<k>`, `-complete`, with any `-2`, `-3`, … collision suffix)" are written as a comma-separated list, but the second and third items omit the `claude/implement-plan-<slug>-` prefix and start with a leading hyphen. A literal reader treats them as full branch names, but no branch literally equals `-validation-fix-<k>` or `-complete`; they are suffixes that have to be appended to the prefix.
  WHY: An implementer running this command and matching branches via `gh api ... pulls/.../files` may filter against the literal names `-validation-fix-<k>` or `-complete` and find no matches, leading to silently dropped branches and an undercounted footprint. The wording needs to show the full prefix on every branch shape (`claude/implement-plan-<slug>-validation-fix-<k>`, `claude/implement-plan-<slug>-complete`) or use a clearly-prefixed shorthand like `claude/implement-plan-<slug>-{validation-fix-<k>|complete}`.

- .claude/commands/audit-plans.md,workflow-templates/.claude/commands/audit-plans.md
  Line or code reference: Report-format section "In-flight /implement-plan-claude work: <implement-plan <slug> (log: <Status:>, stage <Stage:>), PR #M (open, files: …)>  (or: none / logs only — GitHub UNAVAILABLE)" and the "In flight — not candidates" bullet "`<plan> — <orchestrator issue #N / implement-plan <slug>, stage <Stage:>>`" (new lines ~79-82 in the modified file; same text in the workflow-templates copy)
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
  PROBLEM: Both report lines assume every in-flight `/implement-plan-claude` project has a log with `Status:` and `Stage:` lines. For an unlogged PR (slug resolved via the PR's changed files, no log on the default branch yet), there is no Status: or Stage: to fill in.
  WHY: An implementer emitting this line for an unlogged-PR-only project has no values to fill in. They will either render an empty parenthetical (`(log: , stage: )`), omit the parenthetical (deviating from the format), or fabricate values (incorrect). The output is then either awkward or misleading, which is the opposite of "evidence-based" reporting the Rules section demands.

- .claude/commands/audit-plans.md,workflow-templates/.claude/commands/audit-plans.md
  Line or code reference: Step 6, "Build the in-flight footprint", bullet (c) (new lines ~33-36 in the modified file; same text in the workflow-templates copy)
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
  PROBLEM: The rule "once every phase is ticked (`Stage:` is `conformance`, `security-pass`, `validation`, or `completion`), **every file the plan declares**" gates the "all files count" behaviour on a specific set of Stage: values. The conjunction between "every phase is ticked" and "Stage is one of these four" is ambiguous: the parenthetical reads as a clarification (typical stages when all phases are ticked), but the rule literally says the all-files behaviour only fires when Stage matches. A project with all phases ticked but Stage: set to something else (e.g. `blocked`, or a stage the convention has not yet enumerated) would not trigger the all-files rule.
  WHY: The footprint for a fully-ticked project in a non-listed Stage (a real possibility for BLOCKED projects, or for stages added later) would exclude plan files not yet covered by an open PR, allowing a candidate to pass the conflict screen even though its files overlap the still-incoming next-stage changes. The safer rule is "all files count whenever every phase is ticked", with the Stage list as a comment, not a gate.
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_7-plus ===
- .claude/commands/audit-plans.md
  Line or code reference: Step 6 "(b) Open PRs" and report format line "In-flight /implement-plan-claude work: <implement-plan <slug> (log: <Status:>, stage <Stage:>), PR #M (open, files: …)>"
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
  PROBLEM: The report format assumes every `/implement-plan-claude` project has a progress log with `Status:` and `Stage:` lines, but step 6(b) explicitly handles projects found only through open PRs whose log hasn't reached the default branch yet. For such projects, the slug is resolved from the PR's changed files, but no `Status:` or `Stage:` is available to fill into the report format.
  WHY: When executing the command, a project discovered only through an unlogged PR (a new project's first phase PR) has no log on the default branch. The executor knows the project is in flight (from the PR) and has resolved its slug, but cannot fill in the required `Status:` and `Stage:` fields in the report. The format provides no alternative for this case — the "(or: none / logs only — GitHub UNAVAILABLE)" parenthetical covers degraded mode (GitHub unavailable), not the case where GitHub is available but the log hasn't merged yet. The executor must improvise,
